name: The Sicilian Defense
description: The most feared, combative response against 1. e4. Black fights for the center from the flank, aiming for asymmetric, tactical, and unbalanced winning positions.

steps.title: White Opens With e4
steps.explanation: White takes central space and opens diagonals.

steps.title: The Sicilian Strike
steps.explanation: Boom! The Sicilian Defense. We contest the d4 center square using a flank c-pawn, creating an asymmetrical fight from move 1.
steps.warning: Never play 1... c6 or 1... e5 if you intend to play Sicilian lines — 1... c5 defines the board!

steps.title: White Prepares d4
steps.explanation: White prepares to open the center with the d4 pawn thrust.

steps.title: Solidify the Center
steps.explanation: We guard the critical e5 square to prevent White's pawns from advancing, and prepare our knight for f6.

steps.title: The Open Sicilian
steps.explanation: White strikes the center, looking for rapid open piece play.

steps.title: Trade Flank for Center
steps.explanation: The fundamental trade of the Sicilian! We capture White's central d-pawn using our flank c-pawn, giving Black long-term central pawn superiority and the semi-open c-file.

steps.title: White Recaptures
steps.explanation: White places their knight in the center.

steps.title: Attack the e4 Pawn
steps.explanation: We develop our Knight with tempo, immediately attacking White's e4 pawn and forcing White onto the defensive (5. Nc3).
